gemini-2.5-flash.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate experienced an overall deterioration of GBP 6.8m in prior year claims provisions in 2020. This follows an improvement of GBP 36.3m in 2019. The deterioration is attributed to various factors impacting prior years, including catastrophe events like Hurricanes Florence and Michael and California wildfires in 2018, which led to attritional and large losses in Marine and Property lines. Additionally, Covid-19 related event cancellation losses, primarily falling to the 2019 year of account, contributed to the overall adverse development. The 2020 calendar year also saw an unusually active North Atlantic Hurricane season, characterized by frequent, smaller weather losses.

gpt-5-mini.standardized_narrative: The Syndicate's opening gross claims outstanding at 1 January 2020 were GBP 798.7m. During 2020 there was an overall deterioration in prior year reserves of GBP 6.8m, driven primarily by adverse claims development including impacts from natural catastrophe activity (notably US hurricane activity and California wildfires), attritional development in certain marine and liability coverholder accounts, and additional losses related to the Covid-19 pandemic (notably event cancellation in Contingency). The net effect was a modest strengthening of reserves overall, with the largest adverse movements in casualty-related classes and releases in some property and marine classes.
